_comment: THE SHARED PLAN-FILE SELECTION FIXTURE (task sidecar-is-not).
Two independent readers decide which files under plans/ are week PLANS: the engine
load_plans / current_plan / the fast lane) and the gateway (weekly_planner
repo imports the other. Every time one side learned a rule the other did not, a
side-channel file became a plan of record: the parked -dinner-suggestions note drafted
a week titled 'Dinner suggestions for the week of …', and Nora's -review draft was
parsed as the week (prose '## Dinners', zero meals).
This list is the ONE definition both sides are tested against:
The gateway test also compares this list entry-for-entry against its own inline copy,
so a one-sided edit fails there rather than silently re-opening the drift.
CONVENTION: every household plan file is named `<YYYY-WNN>-<role>.md` — the week code
leads. The engine requires that prefix to read a week code at all (stricter than the
gateway's anywhere-in-the-name match); both writers emit the prefix, so every fixture
below is prefix-shaped and the two rules are exercised on the same ground.

candidates.why: an older canonical plan is still a plan
a section companion CONTRIBUTES (flow 35) — it loses selection on content, it is not excluded
a dinner skeleton is a legitimate companion, not an editorial note
the parked side-channel note — never a plan of record
THE INCIDENT — an editorial review with a prose '## Dinners' section
a summary is about the week, not the week
a review OF the family plan is still a review — the role suffix decides, not the substring
